hotspots.title: Patricia Bullrich’s rebellion against Javier Milei
hotspots.blurb: Argentina's Security Minister Patricia Bullrich publicly defied President Javier Milei by refusing to withdraw support for a judicial nominee linked to a critical journalist. This sparked a major internal crisis within the ruling La Libertad Avanza coalition, with Bullrich offering her resignation and exposing deep divisions over governance and judicial appointments.
hotspots.affect: This commands disproportionate attention due to its high-stakes leadership crisis, moral outrage over nepotism allegations, and the potential collapse of the ruling coalition.

hotspots.title: Hungary’s constitutional crisis over president’s removal
hotspots.blurb: Hungary's new Prime Minister Peter Magyar is pushing to amend the constitution to remove President Tamas Sulyok, appointed by Viktor Orban. This move has sparked a constitutional showdown, with Sulyok refusing to resign and Magyar threatening to force his ouster, raising concerns about democratic backsliding and political instability.
hotspots.affect: This commands disproportionate attention due to its high-stakes constitutional crisis, polarized political factions, and the potential erosion of democratic norms in Hungary.

hotspots.title: PP and Vox coalition talks intensify in Spain
hotspots.blurb: Negotiations between Spain's conservative People's Party (PP) and far-right Vox are accelerating across multiple regions, including Castilla y León, Valencia, and Andalusia. Vox is leveraging its influence to push for stricter immigration policies, deregulation, and cuts to cultural and social programs, while PP seeks to maintain stability and avoid early elections.
hotspots.affect: This commands disproportionate attention due to its high-stakes political maneuvering, polarized contention over immigration and regional autonomy, and the potential for far-right influence in Spanish governance.

hotspots.title: Trump administration’s $1.8B anti-weaponization fund scrapped
hotspots.blurb: The Trump administration abandoned its controversial $1.8 billion 'anti-weaponization' fund after facing bipartisan backlash and legal challenges. The fund was intended to compensate allies allegedly targeted by politically motivated investigations, but critics argued it was a slush fund for Trump loyalists, including January 6 defendants.

hotspots.title: Nigel Farage’s racial rhetoric sparks UK outrage
hotspots.blurb: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage faced widespread condemnation after exploiting the murder of student Henry Nowak to push a narrative of 'anti-white prejudice' in the UK. Farage's comments, including the phrase 'white lives matter,' were seen as racially inflammatory and divisive, sparking protests and accusations of stoking racial tensions.
hotspots.affect: This commands disproportionate attention due to its racially charged framing, polarized contention over immigration and policing, and the moral outrage over Farage’s exploitation of a tragic death for political gain.
